answer: Randomized Quorum Partitioning. Each round, a public beacon draws a fresh secret seed and partitions all registered identities into small work groups; only one group, chosen by that seed, may act, and joins are locked before the draw. An attacker cannot precompute which clones land together, so a sparrow of fakes is scattered across groups and any coordinated push is diluted to one group's weight. A mirror identity earns nothing unless its assigned marble surfaces post-draw. Per-identity cost: one full round of idle registration plus forfeited rewards for every unsurfaced marble.
